text: Each feature record feeds a scoring rule. A threshold rule is enough to prove the pipeline end to end — what matters is that scoring consumes one feature record and produces one decision, without that decision getting duplicated downstream.

A risk score combines the rolling transaction count, total amount, and distance since the last transaction into one number, flagging for review above a threshold. Swapping this rule for a trained model later changes nothing around it.
Activator turns a streaming condition into a real action — an alert, a webhook — without hand-rolling the plumbing. Here the condition is 'flagged for review,' firing once per qualifying event.

At-least-once delivery means the same event can arrive twice, and without a safeguard that triggers two alerts. A MERGE keyed on transaction ID makes redelivery a no-op — one alert, no matter how many times the event repeats.
Scoring and alerting are wired, and idempotent by design — exactly why Chapter 1 flagged that requirement before any scoring logic existed. Next up: closing out Project 3 with a retrospective.
